title: Imitation close
hook: a book of short sayings to carry, one a day
tomorrow: can you be holy with a job, a family and a full calendar?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a longing so deep the words run out, and a psalm prayed in two houses. The line was one with him. Today the little book closes.

Thirty days in one little book. Which line will you keep? Not all of them; nobody carries a whole library through a Tuesday. This week alone handed you six, each short enough for a sticky note on a mirror. Nothing sweeter. Four things. Rest above all. The way. Come with reverence. One with him. The Imitation was built for exactly this: sayings small enough to carry, one at a time.
screen: `WHICH LINE WILL YOU KEEP?` → `SIX THIS WEEK ALONE.` → `SMALL ENOUGH TO CARRY.`

segments.voice: Look at how the four books moved. Book one swept the house: other people's words, faults caught early, living as if today. Book two opened the inner door: the kingdom within, peace first, the royal way of the cross. Book three became a conversation, Christ and the disciple talking: love that runs, four loosened grips, rest above every gift, the way you walk. Book four knelt at the altar: reverence, and longing. And here's why one line beats thirty. In book one, the Imitation says to renew your purpose every day, and stir yourself up as if this were the very first day you began. A saying a day is that counsel made small. It isn't a reading plan. It's a way of starting over each morning without shame. The book itself warns against reading to look learned. So the closing move is simple: keep the line that's still working on you.
screen: `BOOK ONE SWEPT THE HOUSE.` · `BOOK TWO OPENED THE INNER DOOR.` · `BOOK THREE BECAME A CONVERSATION.` · `BOOK FOUR KNELT AT THE ALTAR.` · then, large: `A SAYING A DAY.`

segments.voice: Find a pen and a scrap of paper. Let this week's six lines pass slowly through your mind, and notice which one stays when the others drift off. Write that one line by hand, small, and put it somewhere you'll see it tomorrow morning.
Imitation close. The end of our walk through the Imitation of Christ: four books of short sayings, carried one at a time.
Your line: a saying a day. Tomorrow can be the first day again. A little book closes, and a week with it.
